# Establish payment and purchasing approval controls

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before delegating spending or as payment volume and fraud exposure increase. A tested authorization matrix with independently verified payee changes and auditable payment evidence.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Map spending and payment risks

agent-runnable


List purchasing channels, payment accounts, cards, payee-maintenance rights and who currently requests, approves, releases and reconciles payments. Identify cases where one person controls the entire transaction.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve the control design

human · human approval required


Finance leadership sets authority limits, segregation of duties and exception rules suited to team size. Specify independent verification for new or changed bank details and the escalation path for urgent requests.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Configure approved access and approval rules

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


The account administrator implements the approved roles and limits in purchasing and banking systems. Use least-privilege access, retain configuration evidence and protect recovery access from the same person who releases payments.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Test normal and exception transactions

human · human approval required


Walk a small authorized test through request, approval, release and reconciliation. Also test a changed-payee and unavailable-approver scenario without sending funds to an unverified account.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Monitor exceptions and reconcile evidence

agent-runnable


Match released payments to approved invoices and statements. Review overrides and access periodically, record discrepancies and require a new approval for changes outside the original scope.

- Verify: A tested authorization matrix with independently verified payee changes and auditable payment evidence.
- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
